  native:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.14.4'
      - name: Install qualified Clang 20 native execution prerequisites
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          curl --fail --location --retry 3 --output "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-llvm.asc" https://apt.llvm.org/llvm-snapshot.gpg.key
          fingerprint=$(gpg --show-keys --with-colons "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-llvm.asc" | awk -F: '$1 == "fpr" { print $10; exit }')
          test "$fingerprint" = 6084F3CF814B57C1CF12EFD515CF4D18AF4F7421
          sudo install -m 0644 "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-llvm.asc" /usr/share/keyrings/hia-llvm.asc
          printf '%s\n' 'deb [arch=amd64 signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/hia-llvm.asc] https://apt.llvm.org/noble/ llvm-toolchain-noble-20 main' | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/hia-llvm20.list
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y binutils gcc clang-20 libclang-rt-20-dev strace
          printf 'CLANG=/usr/bin/clang-20\nHEPTA_CLANG=/usr/bin/clang-20\n' >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - run: python -m pip install setuptools==78.1.1 wheel==0.46.3 z3-solver==4.15.4.0 jsonschema==4.26.0
      - name: Prepare original locked Rust caller dependencies
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cargo --version
          rustc --version
          sha256sum rust/hia-core-shadow/Cargo.toml rust/hia-core-shadow/Cargo.lock > "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-rust-caller-inputs.sha256"
          cargo fetch --locked --manifest-path rust/hia-core-shadow/Cargo.toml
          sha256sum --check "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-rust-caller-inputs.sha256"
          git diff --exit-code -- rust/hia-core-shadow/Cargo.toml rust/hia-core-shadow/Cargo.lock
      - run: python -B tools/replay_hia_selfhost_cold.py --output "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-cold.json"
      - name: Original call graph and native convergence controls
        run: python -B tools/run_hia_unittest_gate.py tests.test_hia_selfhost_call_graph_efficiency.CallGraphNativeTests
      - run: python -B tests/test_hia_selfhost_language_coverage.py --output "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-language.json"
      - name: Prepare isolated continuation-family evidence
        run: mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-continuation-family"
      - name: Native selected release launch with matching cold and original kernel controls
        run: python -B tools/qualify_hia_release_launch.py --cold-report "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-cold.json" --evidence "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-release-launch-matching-cold"
      - name: Native candidate build with matching cold and all original 55 images
        run: python -B -m tools.qualify_hia_candidate_build --cold-report "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-cold.json" --evidence "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-candidate-build"
      - name: Native Store lifecycle with matching cold and all original controls
        env:
          HEPTA_HIA_STORE_LIFECYCLE_COLD_REPORT: ${{ runner.temp }}/hia-cold.json
          HEPTA_HIA_STORE_LIFECYCLE_EVIDENCE: ${{ runner.temp }}/hia-store-lifecycle
        run: python -B tools/run_hia_unittest_gate.py tests.test_hia_store_lifecycle_native.StoreLifecycleNativeTests
      - name: Native Store lifecycle original agent callers
        run: python -B tools/qualify_hia_store_lifecycle.py --caller-group agent --cold-report "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-cold.json" --evidence "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-store-lifecycle-agent"
      - name: Native Store lifecycle original namespace callers
        run: python -B tools/qualify_hia_store_lifecycle.py --caller-group namespace --cold-report "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-cold.json" --evidence "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-store-lifecycle-namespace"
      - name: Native Store lifecycle original ledger callers
        run: python -B tools/qualify_hia_store_lifecycle.py --caller-group ledger --cold-report "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-cold.json" --evidence "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-store-lifecycle-ledger"
      - name: Native Linux stdio with matching cold and all original 69 controls
        run: python -B tools/qualify_hia_linux_stdio.py --cold-report "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-cold.json" --evidence "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-linux-stdio-matching-cold"
      - name: Native CLI discovery JSON with matching cold and all original four groups
        run: python -B tools/qualify_hia_cli_discovery_json.py --cold-report "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-cold.json" --evidence "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-cli-discovery-json-matching-cold"
      - name: Native linked loader and compiler receipt bindings
        run: |
          python -B - <<'PYBINDINGS'
          from hashlib import sha256
          import json
          import os
          from pathlib import Path
          import unittest
          from tools.build_hia_json_preflight import admit_cold_build
          cold_path = Path(os.environ['HEPTA_HIA_LINKED_OBSERVER_COLD_REPORT'])
          cold_bytes = cold_path.read_bytes()
          cold = json.loads(cold_bytes)
          nested_bytes = Path(cold['nested_report']).read_bytes()
          if sha256(nested_bytes).hexdigest() != cold['nested_report_sha256']:
              raise ValueError('current cold nested report changed before receipt controls')
          nested = json.loads(nested_bytes)
          compiler = Path(nested['generations'][-1]['produced_image'])
          compiler_bytes = compiler.read_bytes()

# HIA discovery JSON component

The explicit discovery image owns the successful capabilities and opcode-catalog
JSON algorithms for the immutable metadata compiled from this source revision.
It selects one of all eight primitive schemas (or default v8), filters fields,
sorts object keys and type arrays, emits the original pretty JSON, constructs
the original canonical form, and computes SHA-256 inside HIA. It stores one
structured metadata table, not nine finished answers or catalog digests.

This component does not switch the ordinary `hia` command. Its fifteen-action
parser, Unicode and color rules, errors, stream encoding and dynamic Python
providers retain their original source bytes. The new API returns UTF-8 JSON
bytes; it is not the old dictionary-returning Python API. Replacing a provider,
mutating its metadata or observing an intermediate dictionary is outside this
new immutable-source component, and remains the responsibility of the unchanged
ordinary entry. No text carrier is substituted for an observable dictionary.

## Build and select

After a real matching-current-source cold qualification has completed, build:

```sh
python tools/build_hia_cli_discovery_json.py --compiler /absolute/cold/B3.image.bin --cold-report /absolute/cold.json --output /absolute/new-discovery-build
```

The builder admits the original outer and nested cold reports, all three actual
equal compiler images, every current cold source and all owner inputs before
creating output. The actual B3 compiles the complete canonical HIA under the
original 20-second and 1 MiB bounds. The native request, receipt, full output,
compiled image and all publication bytes are read back. A separately named
`build_development` Python API records development provenance; the production
qualifier rejects that scope and has no development command-line option.

An explicitly selected local artifact is trusted executable code, not a sandbox
for untrusted images. Select the source-bound image through the installed API:


Every selection rereads the package-owned source, manifest and image. A held

## Buffer contract

The ordinary Core entry is `f0(readbuf, mutbuf, mutbuf) -> u32` with distinct
physical owners. The request contains four little-endian u64 words followed by
the schema bytes: magic `HCLJSON1`, operation (1 capabilities, 2 catalog), mode
(0 absent, 1 explicit), and payload length. An explicit catalog schema is one
of `hepta.hia.program.v1` through v8. Absent catalog schema selects v8.

Workspace is at least 131072 bytes. The public wrapper and original child keep
the existing 1 MiB allocation ceiling. Successful output is the exact pretty
UTF-8 JSON followed by one newline. HIA constructs it in private workspace and
copies only after checking the final output capacity. Output is unchanged on
short output; early request/schema/workspace refusals change no buffer. Status
codes are ffffffff (frame), fffffffe (output), fffffffd (schema), fffffffc
(workspace), and fffffffb (static table bound). These are component statuses,
not an invented substitute for the original CLI diagnostics or exit values.

The toolchain then executes these five stages with the original child and

1. Cold B3 compiles `selfhost_linux_stdio.hepta` to L1.
2. L1 compiles that same captured source to L2.

4. L3 compiles the ordinary `selfhost.hepta`; its complete result must equal B3.
5. L3 compiles the ordinary pure-HIA `linux_stdio_entry_packer.hepta`.

Each program build freshly admits that toolchain, uses L3 to compile the

| `linux.stdin.read` | `mutbuf, usize, usize` | `i64` | `linux_io, write, trap` | One Linux `read` from fd 0 |
| `linux.stdout.write` | `readbuf` or `mutbuf`, then `usize, usize` | `i64` | `linux_io, read, trap` | One Linux `write` to fd 1 |

Attributes must be empty. The second and third operands are offset and count.
The range check proves `offset <= extent` before evaluating
`count <= extent - offset`; an invalid range traps before any external effect.
Read requires a live mutable loan. Write requires a live readable loan. The
existing checker still rejects suspended parents, consumed resources, exclusive
alias conflicts, inconsistent CFG joins, and unbalanced ordinary returns.
The `linux_io` effect propagates through ordinary calls just like the existing
effects. No fabricated helper call is substituted for either instruction.

The signed kernel result is retained without conversion: short transfer, EOF,
zero-length transfer, and negative errno remain distinct. A zero-length operation
still performs its single physical call. The instruction does not retry EINTR,
hide EPIPE, install a signal handler, or convert a foreign Python exception into
an errno. More elaborate retry/publication policy belongs in an HIA program.

## Public admission and reference execution

```python
from hepta.hia_agent_assembly import assemble_program, render_assembly
from hepta.hia_program import verify_program
from hepta.hia_program_runtime import execute_program
from hepta.hia_linux_stdio import PROFILE

checked = assemble_program(source_bytes, profile=PROFILE)
checked_again = verify_program(checked, profile=PROFILE)
canonical_assembly = render_assembly(checked_again, profile=PROFILE)
observed = execute_program(
    checked_again, "f0", (source_bytes_for_f0, output_initial, workspace_initial),
    profile=PROFILE, linux_stdio_provider=physical_observation_provider,
)
```

The profile returns `VerifiedLinuxStdioProgram`, a detached immutable byte
container distinct from `VerifiedProgram`. Its constructor is not an authority:
all consuming entry points recheck its bytes. Default `verify_program`, default
assembly, default scalar VM, default LLVM/Code emission, and default machine
publication refuse this extended input. There is no fallback from a failed
profile build to ordinary Core or from an ordinary call target to a syscall.

The reference VM requires an explicit callable. It never implicitly binds the
real process's stdin or stdout. The callback receives a frozen
`LinuxStdioRequest` containing the fixed descriptor, offset, count, extent and an
immutable copy of the bytes for a write. It receives no pointer, mutable owner,
or capability to change VM storage. It returns an exact `(int, bytes)` tuple.
Negative results are limited to `[-4095, -1]`; positive results may not exceed
count. Read bytes must match the admitted nonnegative result exactly. Write and
negative results carry no returned bytes. Full response validation precedes any
read mutation. Provider exceptions retain their identity.

`LinuxStdioSignal` is an explicit reference observation with an exact built-in
integer signal number. It does not send an OS signal. Its report and provider
refusal reports preserve the actual VM buffers and effect attempt; they are
marked as reference outcomes, not kernel observations or ordinary Core traps.

The `f0` entry uses the existing three-buffer ABI and returns `u32`. Each public
reference input is an exact immutable byte string of at most 1 MiB. The adapter
creates distinct private roots, and only checked internal calls carry loans.
The existing step, heap, and call-depth limits remain. Native compilation retains
the original 128-function, 1536-block, 8192-instruction, 1 MiB
source/output/workspace and 20-second stage limits. Additional native signature,
name, call-graph, and stack constraints remain independently checked by the HIA
compiler; passing the reference checker does not certify native compilability.

## Explicit native construction

The repository construction endpoint is
`tools.build_hia_linux_stdio_program.build_linux_stdio_program`, also available
through its command-line module. It requires an explicit profile, compiler path,
exact lowercase compiler SHA-256, and a new output directory. It never executes
the produced program.

```sh
python -B tools/build_hia_linux_stdio_program.py program.hepta \
  --profile hepta.hia.linux-stdio.v1 \
  --compiler /absolute/path/to/linux-stdio-compiler.image.bin \
  --compiler-sha256 EXACT_SHA256 \
  --output new-build-directory
```

The public parser and typed checker admit the program first. The actual HIA
compiler generates its flat x86-64 image. That compiler also builds the pure HIA
ELF entry packer. The actual packer consumes the exact compiled program and
emits the complete ELF. Every original bounded child receipt is matched against
the outer captured compiler/source/input/output bytes. Final input readbacks,
full ELF structure checks and readback of the executable are mandatory.
No host assembler, host x86 code generator, `.S` template, or opaque startup
image is used by this endpoint.

The ELF has one RX file segment, one RW/NX zero-filled data segment, and an RW/NX
stack declaration. It has no interpreter. The minimal CPU startup establishes
alignment, performs the fixed nondumpable guard, calls the compiled HIA entry,
and exits with its returned word. The actual business read/write and loops are
in HIA. The input view initially has extent zero; output and workspace are each
1 MiB. SIGPIPE disposition is inherited, and the syscall-failure startup path
returns 126 before entering the program. The kernel's observable exit status is
the low eight bits of the returned word.

Construction currently records `EXPLICIT_PINNED_DEVELOPMENT_COMPILER`,
`compiler_provenance_qualified: false`, `matching_cold: false`, and `whole: false`.
A caller pin binds an input; it does not establish its bootstrap provenance.
The author tools, public reference checker/VM, build orchestration and test
supervision remain Python. The produced and tested ELF payload runs directly
under the kernel. These separate facts must not be merged into a whole-system
qualification claim.
